intended_object: The canonical restriction map 𝒪_𝒳(q(V)) → 𝒪_𝒴(V) for the quotient map q : 𝒴 → 𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ (Fargues–Fontaine curve) and an open V ⊆ 𝒴. A section of 𝒪_𝒳 over q(V) is a Frobenius-invariant section of 𝒪_𝒴 over q⁻¹(q(V)), and the map restricts it to V. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is the composite of two maps. The first is `spaXPresheafι` evaluated at q(V). This is the equalizer inclusion 𝒪_𝒳(U) = 𝒪_𝒴(q⁻¹U)^{φ=1} → 𝒪_𝒴(q⁻¹U), i.e. the inclusion into the pushforward q_*𝒪_𝒴. The second is restriction in 𝒪_𝒴 along V ≤ q⁻¹(q(V)), which is the unit of the adjunction between the image and preimage functors on opens for the open map q. This is exactly the standard comparison map that the docstring describes. Later results use it to show that q restricted to a wandering open V is an open immersion, which is how the literature argues as well.

The map depends on this particular construction (Y, X and the Frobenius quotient), so there is no broader generality it should have been stated in. Mathlib has no counterpart for this specific map. It is a canonical morphism with clear mathematical meaning, not a mere implementation detail, and it is defined correctly.
